newsitem.title: USA: Tour finds NW Ohio corn, soybean crops variable.
newsitem.headline: Tour finds NW Ohio corn, soybean crops variable.

text.p: Scouts on one route of the first leg of the Professional Farmers of America corn and soybean tour found variable crop conditions in northwest Ohio.
After surveying crops in five counties, scouts estimated the corn yield potential at anywhere from 80 to 190 bushels per acre.
Last year, the state-wide average yield for Ohio was 111 bushels per acre, the U.S. Agriculture Department said.
The 80-bushel field was found in Defiance County where excessive moisture appeared to have cut the plant population, scouts said.

Tour participants said the other fields scouted had the potential for average to above average yield, given a normal first frost date. The best corn was found in Allen, Hancock and Wood counties in the southern portion of the northwest district, the scouts said.

In Allen County, last year's crop averaged 117.6 bushels per acre, according to USDA data. This year, the number of ears in fields surveyed indicated yield potential would equal or exceed that average.

"For this type of ground we have a good ear count," said Byron Jones, a corn and soybean farmer from McLean County, Illinois. "For the black soils of Illinois and Iowa, that wouldn't be so good but for this soil that's respectable."

Soybean pod counts were also variable but overall they appeared to be average to above average. Scouts said there were no severe problems found in the soybean fields but at the same time, crops did not appear to be exceptionally good.
"This area of Ohio is much better than last year. The crops are more mature than last year," Jones said.
Pod counts were lighter further north, the scouts said.

The Pro Farmer tour will travel through parts of Ohio and Indiana on Tuesday. Scouts will sample fields in Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska and South Dakota before wrapping up in Des Moines on Friday where they will issue estimates for corn and soybean yield potential.
